note: Week 2026-09-08 build. TIMING/HOLIDAY NOTE: the target Monday 2026-09-07 was Labor Day, a US market holiday, so this week is a four-session book running Tue 9/8 through Fri 9/11 and weekStart is set to 9/8. This run also fired late — Tuesday evening 9/8 rather than Sunday — so entries are recorded at the OFFICIAL SIP closes of Tue 9/8, not the prior Friday close. Backdating to the 9/4 close after a full session had already traded would have imported hindsight; the prior-week close-out is still taken at official Fri 9/4 SIP closes, the correct end of that book's hold horizon. PRIOR WEEK: the 8/31-9/4 book snapped a two-week losing streak, closing +790.08 realized (+1.07%) with 6 of 12 names green. HOOD (+15.8%, +700.56) and DELL (+14.0%, +838.50) carried it — DELL's FQ2 print on 9/1 was the AI-server beat the book was positioned for and the stock ran from $459 to $524. PANW was the disaster (-12.8%, -686.42) on a soft FY27 guide, and AVGO (-3.4%) and SLB (-4.2%) gave back their setups. Net: the two binary tech prints split, and the sizing discipline is what made the week positive. THIS WEEK IS ORGANIZED AROUND TWO THINGS. FIRST, THE MIDDLE EAST WAR ESCALATED MATERIALLY OVER THE WEEKEND AND MONDAY. Iran-backed Houthis attacked four cities in southern Saudi Arabia and set oil installations ablaze; the WSJ reported Tuesday that Iran launched an attack on US Navy ships Monday that the military has not acknowledged. WTI settled +1.69% at $93.03 and Brent +0.95% at $97.92, both six-week highs, with Gulf exports already impaired since February's US/Israel strikes and the SPR down to 285.4M barrels — the lowest since November 1982. SECOND, AUGUST CPI LANDS FRIDAY 9/11 AT 8:30AM, four trading days before the 9/15-16 FOMC, with hike odds around 66% after Warsh's Jackson Hole 'we have work to do' keynote and Goldman modeling core at +0.36% against a +0.30% consensus. That is a hot print in the base case and it sits at the very end of the window again. THE BOOK IS BUILT SO THOSE TWO FACTS REINFORCE RATHER THAN FIGHT EACH OTHER. Energy (3 names) is the live catalyst AND the natural CPI hedge: VLO and CVE both closed at fresh 52-week highs Tuesday, CVE and MGY were both upgraded to Overweight at JP Morgan the same morning on a note pointing out oily E&P trades at a 14.1% 2026 FCF yield versus 9.3% for gas, with MGY's upgrade specifically on accretion from the $4.1B WildFire deal that doubles its Giddings position. INDUSTRIALS (3 names) is the war-and-power leg: LMT was upgraded to Buy at UBS with a $674 target on a 9% revenue CAGR through 2028 in missiles and munitions that UBS says is not priced in, GEV announced an $11.75B acquisition of Consolidated Precision Products from Warburg Pincus and Berkshire and closed 2.8% above its open on it, and ETN carries the UBS Buy upgrade and $515 target on a Q3 margin inflection. TECHNOLOGY (3 names) deliberately carries only ONE binary event: ORCL reports FQ1 Thursday AMC with $638B of RPO and options implying an 11% move, and it is entered 53% below its September 2025 high rather than at it. The other two tech names are thematic with confirming volume and no scheduled event — COHR on the 800G/1.6T optical scale-up cycle that OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra release put back in play, and INTC on Northland's upgrade to Outperform with a $120 target into a genuine server-CPU shortage, which traded 140M shares against an 82M average. MTB is the single financial and is held BECAUSE of the hike: Morgan Stanley named it a top pick Tuesday with a $304 target on an NII beat-and-raise it thinks the Street is underwriting, and it is 12.7x earnings at 1.36x book. CPRT is the consumer name and the second in-window print (FQ4 Thursday AMC), bought 34% below its 52-week high near the July low rather than into strength. AZN is the lone healthcare name, added on the day XLV was dumped on two Novartis failures — its own news was the opposite, a Phase 3 overall-survival win for Imfinzi plus Amgen's Imdelltra in first-line extensive-stage small cell lung cancer. WHAT WAS DELIBERATELY LEFT OUT: QCOM, despite the $4B Amazon warrant and custom-AI-chip deal, reversed from $183.49 to close at $174.09 on 2.6x volume — that is a distribution day, not a breakout. MU faded from $1,036.70 to $1,000.26 despite UBS calling DRAM and NAND undersupplied into 2027. HOOD printed a bearish outside day after last week's 15.8% run and its Crypto.com event-contracts deal, so last week's winner was taken off rather than pressed. ADBE reports the same night as ORCL and was skipped precisely to avoid two binaries on one evening. 12 names, 86.8% deployed, 13.2% cash held wide for Friday's CPI.

positions.name: Valero Energy
positions.catalyst: Closed Tuesday 9/8 at $382.85, a fresh 52-week high set the same session ($384.26 intraday), as WTI settled +1.69% at $93.03 and Brent +0.95% at $97.92 — both six-week highs — after Iran-backed Houthis attacked four cities in southern Saudi Arabia and set oil installations ablaze. Gulf crude exports have been impaired since February's US/Israel strikes on Iranian energy infrastructure and shipping through Hormuz, and the US SPR fell another 1.2M barrels to 285.4M, the lowest level since November 1982. Refining crack spreads are the direct beneficiary of constrained product supply, and VLO is still only 15.4x earnings.
positions.risks: Sitting exactly at a 52-week high with zero cushion; any Middle East de-escalation headline unwinds the whole energy leg at once; a very hot CPI Friday that is driven by energy would be good for the stock and bad for the other nine names, so this is a hedge that only pays on one axis.
positions.driver: Cheapest large-cap way to own constrained refined-product supply, breaking to a 52-week high on the day the catalyst escalated.

positions.name: Cenovus Energy
positions.catalyst: Upgraded to Overweight from Neutral at JP Morgan on Tuesday morning 9/8, and closed at $33.19 — a fresh 52-week high, with the intraday high of $33.78 also set that session. JPM's note says its oily E&P coverage trades at 2026-27 FCF yields of 14.1%/13.5% versus 9.3%/10.3% for gas coverage and sees 5% and 3% upside to consensus 2026-27 EBITDA. The CVE call specifically cites an asset footprint that captures BOTH crude strength and refining margin strength as an integrated, which is the exact configuration this tape rewards.
positions.risks: At its 52-week high on the day of the upgrade, so the easy money on the call may already be made; Canadian heavy differentials can widen independently of Brent; Trump's trade rhetoric toward Canada was an explicit market headwind Tuesday and a tariff headline would hit a Calgary-domiciled name hardest.
positions.driver: Same-day Overweight upgrade from a major bank landing on a 52-week-high breakout, at 12.4x earnings.

positions.name: Magnolia Oil & Gas
positions.catalyst: Also upgraded to Overweight from Neutral at JP Morgan on Tuesday 9/8, with the upgrade explicitly attributed to anticipated accretion from the recently closed $4.1B WildFire acquisition, which doubles Magnolia's Giddings position in the Austin Chalk. Traded 5.88M shares against a 2.96M 30-day average — roughly 2x confirming volume. At 11.7x earnings and 2.29x book with a 2.5% yield, and unlike the other two energy names it is 16% BELOW its 52-week high of $32.76, so the crude move is not yet in the price.
positions.risks: $6.5B market cap makes it the smallest name in the book and the most gap-prone; pure E&P beta means it is the first thing sold on a de-escalation headline; integration risk on a deal that doubles the asset base; a hawkish CPI compresses small-cap multiples fastest.
positions.driver: The only energy name entered with meaningful room to its own 52-week high, on a same-day upgrade with 2x volume confirmation.

positions.name: Oracle
positions.catalyst: FQ1 2027 results Thursday 9/10 after the close — the single largest scheduled event of the window. Consensus is roughly $19.13B revenue (+28.1% YoY) and non-GAAP EPS near $1.74 (+18.4%), against $638B of remaining performance obligations and management guidance for 58-64% YoY cloud order growth. Options are implying an 11% move, which is actually below Oracle's own historical average. The stock traded 37.7M shares Tuesday versus a 20.9M average.
positions.risks: Genuinely binary, and the setup is a falling knife — the stock is down 53% from its $345.72 high of September 2025 and only 42% above its $114.50 July low, meaning the market has already repriced the AI-capex-funded RPO story once. The bear case is that RPO converts to revenue more slowly than guided while capex keeps compounding; a miss on OCI margin recovery is the obvious way this breaks.
positions.driver: The marquee in-window print, entered 53% below the high rather than into strength, and sized so an 11% adverse move costs the book under 1%.

positions.name: Coherent Corp.
positions.catalyst: Rose 6.9% Tuesday from a $282.13 open to a $301.88 close on 8.70M shares against a 5.13M two-week average, leading a broad optical-component rally (with LITE, CIEN and AAOI) driven by commentary following OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra release on 9/3. Copper reach and power become limiting constraints at 800G and 1.6T, so another compute-scale-up cycle forces hyperscalers into more high-speed optical transceivers, lasers and photonics — and Coherent is one of the few US suppliers of those parts at scale, on top of an already capacity-constrained AI-optics backdrop.
positions.risks: 68x earnings with no in-window event to validate the move, so this is pure thematic momentum; the group has run hard and Tuesday's candle closed off its $315.70 high; global chip sales fell 9.8% month-on-month in July per SIA, so the underlying semi tape is not uniformly strong.
positions.driver: Best risk/reward in the optical complex — same thematic bid as LITE but entered 31% below its own 52-week high instead of near it.

positions.name: Intel
positions.catalyst: Upgraded to Outperform at Northland on Tuesday 9/8 with a $120 price target, on the argument that Intel has made material progress on the turnaround AND that a genuine shortage of server CPUs is now benefiting the company. The stock rose 3.6% from a $100.85 open to a $104.47 close on 140.3M shares against an 81.95M two-week average — 1.7x confirming volume, and the largest dollar volume in the book. The supply-shortage thesis is corroborated by UBS's same-day note that DRAM and NAND remain undersupplied into 2027 with DDR contract prices up 22% quarter-on-quarter.
positions.risks: Still loss-making on a trailing basis, so the multiple is unanchored; the turnaround has produced several false starts already; at $104.47 it is up more than 4x from the $24.05 low of September 2025, which is a lot of recovery to have already banked; no scheduled event in-window to confirm the shortage narrative.
positions.driver: Fresh upgrade plus a supply-shortage thesis independently corroborated the same day, with the strongest volume confirmation of any name in the book.

positions.name: Lockheed Martin
positions.catalyst: Upgraded to Buy from Neutral at UBS on Tuesday 9/8 with the target raised to $674 from $581 — roughly 26% above the entry — on growth in missiles and munitions plus F-35 sustainment, CH-53K and Trident driving a 9% revenue CAGR through 2028 that UBS says is above consensus and does not appear priced in. The upgrade landed on the same day the WSJ reported Iran attacked US Navy ships on Monday and Houthi forces struck Saudi energy facilities, which is the munitions-consumption catalyst the thesis needs.
positions.risks: Defense primes are budget-cycle stories, not war-headline stories, so the geopolitical link is looser than it looks; at 19.4x with a 13.8x price-to-book the valuation is not cheap on assets; the stock has been in a downtrend since the $692 March high and this is a counter-trend entry.
positions.driver: Largest-percentage sell-side target raise of the day, arriving on the exact day the underlying demand catalyst escalated.

positions.name: GE Vernova
positions.catalyst: Announced Tuesday 9/8 that it will acquire castings maker Consolidated Precision Products from Warburg Pincus and Berkshire Partners for $11.75B, vertically integrating a critical supply input for gas turbines and aerospace components at exactly the moment turbine lead times are the binding constraint on data-center power. The market endorsed it: the stock opened at $945.02 and closed at $971.31, up 2.8% from the open and within $3 of the session high, on a day the S&P fell 0.58%. Nuclear and power names broadly outperformed.
positions.risks: Acquirers usually de-rate, and $11.75B is a large check; 27x earnings and a 21x price-to-book leave no margin for integration slippage; the stock is still 19% below its $1,195.94 July high, so the trend has been down since summer; no in-window event to re-rate it.
positions.driver: Same-day M&A that the market voted for — closing 2.8% above the open, near the high, on a down tape.

positions.name: Eaton Corp.
positions.catalyst: Upgraded to Buy from Neutral at UBS on Tuesday 9/8 with the target raised to $515 from $450 — about 22% upside — on strong sales growth and an expectation that margins improve meaningfully in Q3 and beyond on proactive pricing and better execution. The call sits inside the broadest theme in the market: Barclays raised its 2026 capex growth estimate to +19% from +15% in July and lifted industrial-tech targets across the board the same morning, and electrical equipment is the direct beneficiary of data-center buildout.
positions.risks: Weakest price confirmation in the book — it faded from a $430.25 high to close at $422.13, essentially flat and below its open, despite the upgrade, which means the market did not endorse the call; 41.8x earnings is the second-richest multiple here; no in-window event.
positions.driver: Smallest position in the book by design: a fresh upgrade with real upside on a name bought flat rather than chased, in the theme with the most durable spending behind it.

positions.name: M&T Bank
positions.catalyst: Morgan Stanley upgraded M&T to Overweight on Tuesday 9/8, named it a TOP PICK, and raised its target to $304 from $253 — calling it a beat-and-raise story on net interest income as loan growth accelerates, with a buyback story in 2027 the firm says remains underappreciated. Critically, this is the one name in the book that is HELPED by the September hike: with odds around 66% into the 9/15-16 FOMC, a higher policy rate lifts asset yields on a bank whose funding base is already repriced. It trades at 12.7x earnings and 1.36x book.
positions.risks: Bought on a down day — it opened at $242.49 and closed at $238.44 as financials sold off with the broader tape; if CPI comes in soft and the hike is priced out, the entire thesis inverts; regional-bank credit remains the tail risk nobody can underwrite from outside.
positions.driver: The book's explicit hedge against its own biggest risk: a top-pick upgrade on a cheap bank that gains from the CPI outcome that hurts everything else here.

positions.name: Copart
positions.catalyst: FQ4 2026 results Thursday 9/10 after the close, consensus $0.38 EPS — the second and last binary event in the book, deliberately placed in a different sector from the first. The setup is the opposite of a chase: at $32.60 the stock is 33.7% below its $49.16 high of September 2025 and only 8% above the $26.81 low set on 7/23/26, at 21x earnings for a business with structurally high returns on capital. The Manheim Used Vehicle Value Index printed 208.2 for August, up 0.4% year-over-year, which supports salvage auction pricing.
positions.risks: Binary, and Copart has missed on volume growth in recent quarters; insurance-carrier total-loss frequency is the swing variable and it is outside management's control; a stock this far off its highs is off them for a reason, and a fourth consecutive disappointing print would take out the July low.
positions.driver: In-window print bought near a 52-week low rather than a high — the cheapest expression of a quality compounder in the book.

positions.name: AstraZeneca
positions.catalyst: Announced Tuesday 9/8 that Imfinzi combined with Amgen's Imdelltra significantly improved overall survival in first-line extensive-stage small cell lung cancer — a Phase 3 overall-survival win in an indication with very poor standard-of-care outcomes. The timing is what makes it interesting: healthcare was the WORST sector Tuesday, dumped wholesale after Novartis reported two separate Phase 3 failures (pelacarsen in the HORIZON cardiovascular study and del-desiran in the HARBOR myotonic dystrophy study), dragging AMGN, IONS, SRPT, DYN and NAMS down with it. AZN's own news pointed the other way and the stock was sold anyway.
positions.risks: Bought into a sector the market is actively de-rating, and sentiment beats single-asset data in the short run; the stock closed at $160.04, only 9.8% above its $145.79 52-week low and 25% below the February high, so the downtrend is intact; overall-survival data does not convert to revenue inside a four-day window.
positions.driver: The only name in the book bought on a sector-wide dislocation rather than momentum — positive company-specific Phase 3 data on the day its sector was liquidated.
